output.summary: The labour-market evidence argues predominantly for a hold, with only a faint hawkish tilt. The pre-read shows unemployment (4.2) exactly at the natural rate (u_star 4.2) with a 0.0 gap, a very low Sahm reading (0.033) and subdued claims (197.8k / 206.7k), signalling no slack and no deterioration that would justify a cut. The SEP unemployment path is flat at 4.1 percent and was revised down from 4.3 percent, reinforcing a resilient labour market. Offsetting this, payroll gains (3m 50.7k, 12m 41.3k) run well below the 75.0k breakeven, a cooling signal that leans against additional tightening. Both July and September statements call job gains in step with the workforce and the unemployment rate little changed. Net: a balanced labour market pointing to a hold, nudged marginally hawkish by low claims and downward-revised unemployment projections.
